$comment: Canonical design tokens for Argentum. This file is the source; the dashboard's
CSS variables and the backend's Go report theme are generated from it by
`make tokens` and committed. Never hand-edit a generated file — CI diffs it.
Keys beginning with $ are documentation and are ignored by the generators.
`scope` decides which generators see a group:
all   → both the dashboard CSS and the Go report theme
web   → dashboard CSS only (chrome that has no meaning on paper)
print → Go report theme only (units the browser has no use for)
Colours are hex because hex is what a designer reads and what Go needs. The
CSS generator converts to the bare `H S% L%` triples shadcn/ui expects.
Light palette only: documents are printed and forwarded, so the dark palette
has no meaning on paper and stays hand-written in the dashboard's index.css.

background.doc: Page background (cream). Large fills, PDF page background.

surface.doc: Cards, inputs, table bands — anything that sits on the background.

surfaceMuted.doc: Slightly darker cream: hover states, alternating table rows.

surfaceSubtle.doc: Quietest fill: disabled controls, table header band, callout backgrounds.

primary.doc: Brand accent. Rules, KPI emphasis, focus ring, chart series 1.

primaryForeground.doc: Text and icons on a primary fill.

muted.doc: Secondary text: captions, footers, page numbers, chart axis labels.

sidebarSurface.doc: Sidebar background — matches the chat composer, not the page cream.

sidebarAccentForeground.doc: Sidebar text on a hover fill.

$comment: One family, two roles — the dashboard has always used Space Grotesk for
both. `family` is the CSS name; `key` is the identifier the Go renderer
registers with maroto's font repository. Space Grotesk ships no italic
face, which is why there is no italic key: see fonts.go.

medium.doc: Table headers and labels. A separate maroto family because maroto's style set is normal/bold/italic only — there is no weight axis to put 500 on.

radius.$comment: One radius. `rem` is what the browser uses; `mm` is the same 12px at 96dpi, for rounded callouts and KPI cards in print.

$comment: Print units (pt), because this scale exists for the document renderer.
The dashboard's scale is Tailwind's and stays there: emitting pt-based
font sizes into CSS would be a unit error, not a shared token.

caption.doc: Footer, page numbers, chart axis labels, callout meta.

spacing.$comment: Millimetres, for page layout. The dashboard uses Tailwind's spacing scale.

sm.doc: Between a heading and its paragraph.

$comment: Page geometry. Not shared with the web, but it lives here so that a
margin change is one edit with a CI drift check behind it, the same as a
colour change. A4 because every customer of this product is outside the
United States; Letter would be the exception, not the default.

hairline.doc: Table rules and dividers. Below ~0.15mm a rule disappears on an office laser printer.

$comment: Categorical series palette for T-R3, ordered by series index: series 1 is
the brand red, and the order after that is chosen so a 2- or 3-series
chart gets the widest separation available.
Method: every entry sits on a rung of a CIE L* ladder spanning 24→82 with
a minimum pairwise gap of 6.5 L* (the tightest pair is red 59.3 vs green
65.7, which only co-occur in an 8-series chart). L* is the greyscale axis,
so the ladder is what makes the palette survive a black-and-white
printer, and it is also what carries the red/green pairs through
deuteranopia — hue collapses, lightness does not. Hues are then spread
around the wheel so colour, not just lightness, does the work for readers
with normal vision. T-R3 owns the formal CVD and greyscale verification.
Only `hex` and `doc` are read by the generator; `lStar` is recorded so a
future edit can see the ladder it is standing on. Recompute with
`pnpm --filter @argentum/design-tokens run palette`.
